# Accessibility Statement Template

An accessibility statement publicly describes your commitment to accessibility,
your conformance level, known limitations, and how users can report problems or
get help. Some laws require one; it's good practice everywhere. Adapt the
placeholders. See [accessibility law](../10-legal-and-compliance/accessibility-law.md).

> ⚖️ Adapt to your real situation and jurisdiction; a false claim of conformance
> can backfire. State only what's true.

---

# Accessibility Statement for [WEBSITE / ORGANIZATION NAME]

**Last updated: [DATE]**

## Our commitment

[ORGANIZATION NAME] is committed to ensuring digital accessibility for people
with disabilities. We are continually improving the user experience for everyone
and applying the relevant accessibility standards.

## Conformance status

The [Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/wcag/)
define requirements for designers and developers to improve accessibility for
people with disabilities. It defines three levels of conformance: Level A, Level
AA, and Level AAA.

This website is **[fully / partially] conformant with WCAG [2.2] Level [AA]**.
*[“Partially conformant” means some parts of the content do not fully conform to
the accessibility standard.]*

## Measures we take

[ORGANIZATION NAME] takes the following measures to ensure accessibility:

- [e.g., Accessibility is included in our design and development process.]
- [e.g., We test with automated tools and manual keyboard/screen‑reader checks.]
- [e.g., We provide accessibility training to our team.]
- [e.g., We review accessibility periodically as part of maintenance.]

## Known limitations

Despite our efforts, some content may not yet be fully accessible. Known issues
include:

- [Describe known limitation, the impact, and the plan/timeline to fix — or state
  “We are not currently aware of any accessibility barriers.”]

## Compatibility

This site is designed to be compatible with recent versions of major browsers
and assistive technologies, including [e.g., screen readers such as NVDA,
VoiceOver, and JAWS]. [Note any known incompatibilities.]

## Feedback — tell us about barriers

We welcome your feedback on the accessibility of this website. If you encounter
a barrier or need content in an alternative format, please contact us:

- **Email:** [ACCESSIBILITY EMAIL]
- **Phone:** [PHONE]
- **Postal address:** [ADDRESS]

We aim to respond within [e.g., 5 business days].

## Enforcement / escalation

*[Where required — e.g., EU/UK public sector — include the relevant enforcement
body and how to escalate a complaint.]*

If you are not satisfied with our response, you can contact [RELEVANT BODY /
REGULATOR].
